![](images/d8/d8fd52f3c965f041ea3e9bbc4e8a9705c49ec95be105653d869a0443fa97fac9.png)

The diagram above shows a circle of radius $r$ centered at the origin. If the polar coordinates of the point $A$ are $(8, \frac{π}{4})$ and $m∠AOB = \frac{5π}{12}$, what are the Cartesian coordinates of $B$?
corrected_content.worked_solution: The diagram puts $B$ counterclockwise from $A$ in the second quadrant. Its angle is $\pi/4+5\pi/12=2\pi/3$ and its radius is $8$. Therefore $$B=(8\cos(2\pi/3),8\sin(2\pi/3))=(-4,4\sqrt3).$$
